description.narrative: The Direct Aid Program (DAP) is a small grants program funded by the Australian Government and managed by the Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade (DFAT) overseas posts. It sits alongside Australia's longer-term country and multilateral development strategies, and with its wide geographical reach plays an important role in supporting local community efforts towards poverty reduction and sustainable development across the globe, consistent with Australia's national interest.

title.narrative: Who can apply for DAP funding?

description.narrative: Access to clean water remains a serious challenge in remote parts of Paraguay, particularly during periods of drought. With support from the Australian Direct Aid Program, the Paraguayan NGO Tierra Libre Instituto Social y Ambiental implemented a project to provide safe drinking water to students in the remote Indigenous community of Nivacle Fischat. The initiative involved installing over 50 metres of guttering and three large water tanks—each with a capacity of 30,000 litres—at the local school, ensuring a reliable water supply for more than 200 students and teachers. In times of drought, the system will also serve the broader community of 1,200 people. To ensure the long-term sustainability of the project, community members received training in water management and maintenance, helping to safeguard water quality and promote local ownership.

title.narrative: Climate adaptation, mitigation, environment and biodiversity

description.narrative: DAP provided funding to support the Female Foresters Association to reforest five hectares of land in the semi-arid region of Kaffrine in central Senegal, where desertification and deforestation are escalating. An inability to afford seeds, coupled with a broken irrigation system has adversely affected the production capacity of the sixty-member association. In addition to supporting members’ families, the association plays a vital role in environmental conservation in the region. ‍ The project, which began in April this year, will expand the production capacity of the female foresters from 50,000 to 200,000 plants within a year and double their monthly incomes from 30,000 (AUD81)FCFA to 60,000 FCFA (AUD162 ).

Gender-based violence and harassment remain persistent challenges in Argentina, particularly affecting women in low-income employment. With support from the Australian Direct Aid Program, the Argentine NGO Grow implemented a project in Buenos Aires and Córdoba to address this issue. The initiative collaborated with employers to develop workplace policies and procedures aimed at preventing gen-der-based violence and harassment. Additionally, the project provided training to over 800 women in low-income sectors, raising awareness of their rights and informing them about available support mechanisms in cases of violence or harassment.

The Australian Embassy in Belgrade supported innovative online platform OsnaŽene.com (Empowered.com), designed for continued growth and collaboration among women entrepreneurs. Through the project, 100 women entrepreneurs, aged 35-57, from across Serbia, particularly those in rural and underrepresented communities were empowered by strengthening their digital and entrepreneurial skills. ‍ Through online workshops and a tailored mentorship program, participants gained knowledge in e-commerce, marketing, sales and time management. All 100 women created business profiles and uploaded products to the newly developed OsnaŽene.com web shop, giving them a lasting online presence and access to wider markets. For some, this experience was transformative. “I never imagined I could present my handmade products online. Now I see new possibilities”, said one of the participants. ‍ The project addressed key barriers to economic participation by providing free access to the digital platform and shop and continues mentorship support. ‍ As a result, many women received their first online orders, some from abroad, while others reported increased self-confidence and improved business practices. A strong peer community emerged, fostering ongoing support and collaboration. ‍ The initiative directly advanced Australia’s gender equality and women’ empowerment objectives, demonstrating how targeted support can build sustainable economic resilience and digital empowerment for women entrepreneurs.

The Australian Government , through its Direct Aid Program partnered with a local NGO for the provision of medical equipment (mainly respiratory equipment) to support preterm babies at Mbuya Nehanda Maternity Hospital located at Parirenyatwa Group of Hospitals which is Zimbabwe’s largest referral hospital. ‍ The equipment is being used at the hospital’s Neonatal Intensive Care Unit (NICU) and the Immediate Kangaroo Mother Care Unit (IKMC). ‍ The Australian Government’s contribution has assisted the hospital to: ‍ 1. Improve its capacity to admit and provide care for more preterm babies. ‍ 2. Optimise the management of admitted preterm babies. ‍ 3. Improve the standard and quality of care provided to preterm babies at the hospital. ‍ 4. Improve the survival rate of preterm babies at the hospital from 51% to 66% (since April 2024).

description.narrative: The Australian Government, through its Direct Aid Program in Harare, supported the installation of a borehole for Dobi Primary School which is located in a rural area in Matobo District in Matabeleland South Zimbabwe. ‍ The borehole has improved access to safe drinking water for 223 individuals comprising students and teachers at Dobi Primary School (specifically 117 females and 106 males). Prior to installation of the borehole the school did not have a water source of its own and had to rely on an offsite congested community borehole and unprotected wells. ‍ The project is also enabling access to clean water for an estimated 30 community households that are in close proximity to the school following the establishment of water access point just outside the school premises.

description.narrative: Through the 2024-25 funding round of our Direct Aid Program, the Australian High Commission in Abuja supported the work of Africa Nature Investors Foundation (ANI), a conservation-focused NGO in eastern Nigeria, working to protect Nigeria’s national parks. ‍ Our partnership supported the installation of off-grid electrification for 63 households in Mayo-Selbe village, adjacent to Gashaka Gumti National Park. Delivered in collaboration with Australian energy technology company Okra Solar, the project used new mesh-grid systems to provide power to homes, small businesses, and a primary health clinic serving over 2,500 people for the first time. Improved energy access through the project has strengthened local livelihoods, helped ANI build support for its conservation efforts and promoted an innovative Australian renewable energy solution.

With support from the Australian Direct Aid Program, the Argentine NGO FEIM launched a project aimed at preventing early child marriage. Central to the initiative was the training of key stakeholders and decision-makers in the use of the Early Union Risk Prediction Index—a tool designed to identify children at risk of early marriage. Through this project, awareness of gender rights was significantly increased, and the capacity of local institutions was strengthened, enabling them to more effectively detect and prevent early unions.
